object_description: large three-story volume with a flat roof and covered entrance
design_condition: The building is placed orthogonally in the southeast corner of the leveled site, extending east–west close to the western neighbor while preserving distance to the north, with retaining walls enclosing the plot.

positive.statement: The urban and volumetric approach is promising.
The placement creates a pleasantly large distance from the northern plot.
A second obstacle-free entrance is provided further to the west.
The two upper floors are clearly structured around a central core.
The material rooms are easily accessible.
All three basic-level classes have an overview of the entire outdoor space.
The simple supporting structure with direct load transfer corresponds to an economic principle.

negative.statement: The retaining walls around the leveled site appear unfortunate in relation to the neighboring plots.
The large-looking building and its windows, which are too small, weaken the architectural expression.
The wooden facade seems strange in the neighborhood.
The covered entrance situation is only formulated schematically.
The usage distribution is not optimal and the entrance area is too small.
The basic-level zones are not very flexible and are connected only through vertical access.
The relationship between the teachers' room and teachers' cloakroom does not make sense.
More direct access to the outdoor space would be desirable for all units.
The window treatment makes communication with children outside more difficult.
The outdoor landscape leaves too little space for free movement and lacks a suitable field of activity for discovery games.
The construction volume is comparatively large and entails higher gray energy.
The expected construction costs are in the upper range of the shortlisted projects.
The rooms have limited and sometimes insufficient daylight.
The implementation has significant deficits in access, fenestration, and design integration into the district.
